messages.subject: Fwd: Spatial Capture-Recapture Workshop
messages.body_plain:
Metode ulova in ponovnega ulova se izvaja na pasteh, do nedavnega pa se prostorski kontekst skoraj ni upošteval. Zaradi problema roba so iznašli nekaj "ad hoc" rešitev (če vas zanima kaj več o tem, me  pocukajte za rokav, ker je tema mojega doktorata), za celostno rešitev pa so razvili MCMC modele, ki uporabljajo lokacijo pasti (+ nekaj predpostavk) neposredno. Po domače povedano, neka statistika, ki je povezana s predpostavkami in oddaljenostjo od pasti, je vključena v verjetje (angl. likelihood).
V knjigi Spatial capture-recapture so lepo predstavljeni MCMC in kako jih lahko ocenimo z veliko R kode. Če poznate koga, ki bi se želel udeleži delavnice, kjer bodo predstavljeni modeli iz knjige, je to dobra priložnost, da spoznate ustanovne očete teh metod.
MCMC verige se poganja v WinBUGS/JAGS, se pa vse ostalo dogaja v R-ju.

lp,
Roman

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Richard Chandler <rcha...@warnell.uga.edu>
Date: Fri, Feb 12, 2016 at 6:10 PM
Subject: Spatial Capture-Recapture Workshop
To: Unmarked package <unma...@googlegroups.com>, "spatialcapture." <spatialcapt...@googlegroups.com>, "hmec...@googlegroups.com" <hmec...@googlegroups.com>

Hi everyone,

Andy Royle and I will be offering a SCR workshop at UGA in July. Details below.

Richard

Instructors
Andy Royle (Patuxent Wildlife Research Center)
Richard Chandler (University of Georgia)

Date: 12-15 July 2016 (4 days)

Location: Athens, Georgia

Overview
This course will introduce key models used in the analysis of spatially-explicit capture-recapture data, following closely material from the book “Spatial Capture-Recapture <http://store.elsevier.com/Spatial-Capture-Recapture/J_-Royle/isbn-9780124059399/>” (Elsevier, 2014). Participants will learn how to estimate population parameters and model spatial and temporal variation in density and vital rates using a variety of data types, including data from camera traps, hair snares, live traps, and mist-nets. Models to be covered include closed and open population models, models of landscape resistance, mark-resight models, and integrated population models. Software coverage will include the R packages “secr” and “oSCR” as well as JAGS and WinBUGS.

Course requirements:
This is an intermediate-level workshop with topical lectures followed by work sessions where we analyze data and solve exercises. Participants should have (1) good working knowledge of modern regression methods (regression, ANOVA, generalized linear models, random effects); (2) experience analyzing data in R; (3) familiarity with using WinBUGS or JAGS; (4) knowledge of basic capture-recapture concepts and methods.

Computers
People must bring laptop with a recent version of R, WinBUGS and/or JAGS installed and functional

Cost
USD$550 (normal rate), USD$350 (student rate), which includes lunch, refreshment breaks, and instructional materials.

Registration information and additional information about the workshop can be found here: http://conted.warnell.uga.edu/courses/cap-recap2016

--
Richard Chandler
Assistant Professor
Warnell School of Forestry and Natural Resources
University of Georgia
706-542-5815
Lab website <http://chandlerlab.wordpress.com>

messages.body_plain:
Z zadnjo verzijo 2.0.0 je paket adegenet doživel kar nekaj sprememb. Zaradi manj bolečin v prihodnosti in zavoljo konsistentnosti je tudi pokvaril kar nekaj kode, in nekateri so to že občutili. :)

2.0.0 je pomembna tudi s tega vidika, da se je razvoj preselil na priljubljeno omrežje GitHub (https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/), kjer lahko vsak brez večjega napora predlaga spremembe in dodatke.

Včeraj pa je bila na CRAN sprejeta nova vmesna različica 2.0.1 s kar nekaj pomembnimi popravki in tudi kakim cukrčkom.

https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/releases/tag/2.0.1

lp,
Roman

--

Subject: februarsko predavanje (za las)

Hypotheses testing: is it good for science?

Datum dogodka:

ponedeljek, 29 Februar, 2016 - 13:00

Lokacija predavanja:

IBMI

Predavatelj:

dr. Francesco Pauli

Despite being a standard tool for data analysis in many scientific fields, statistical testing has always been associated to criticism and controversies. Recently, the debate on the role of statistical testing in science has been particularly vivid and coupled with the debate on the lack of reproducibility of scientific results in many disciplines. We review some recent critics and purported consequences of statistical testing use and abuse and discuss proposed remedies, which entails either improving testing or abandoning it for alternative, more appropriate, strategies.

messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] rCharts in RMarkdown
messages.body_plain:
Zdravo,

sem probal skoraj vse haklce (razen na roke pletel rezultat preko pandoca), ki jih priporočajo na internetsih, pa nekako noben ne primer. Predlagam, da odpreš nov "issue" na Ramnathovem GitHub repozitoriju za rCharts.

Ena rešitev, ki uspe producirati sliko je, da shraniš graf kot "standalone" <https://github.com/ramnathv/rCharts/issues/492#issuecomment-52111192>. To ima za pomanjkljivost, da zadeva ni "inline" in ne moreš na preprost način (mogoče se da na roke skopirat graf in vse potrebne elemente v končni html) producirat avtomagičnega markdown dokumenta.

lp,
Roman
